1. In class, we used the **nCoV\_simple** dataset and fit normal, lognormal and gamma models.  Fit a Weibull model to the same dataset and answer the following questions.

    a. What are the parameter estimates of the Weibull model?
    
    b. What is the log likelihood of the Weibull model?  Calculate this likelihood using the formula first and then verify your result with the value given by **fitdistr**.   
    
    c. Write down the log likelihood of the normal, lognormal, and gamma models we used in class.  Based on the log likelihood, which model is the best fit?
    
    
    d. Using the Weibull model and the estimated parameters, what is the probability that the incubation period is shorter than 14 days?  What is the probability that the incubation period is longer than 5 days?


<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library('MASS')
ncov_simple <- read.csv('../all_lectures/nCoV_simple.csv')
result <- fitdistr(ncov_simple$incubation,'weibull')
result$estimate
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   shape    scale 
1.819250 4.611153 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
result$loglik
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] -109.5789
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
log(prod(dweibull(ncov_simple$incubation,
               shape=result$estimate[1],
               scale=result$estimate[2]))) #by hand
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] -109.5789
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
pweibull(14,shape=result$estimate[1],scale=result$estimate[2])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 0.9994694
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
1-pweibull(5,shape=result$estimate[1],scale=result$estimate[2])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 0.3138984
```


:::
:::


For (c): The loglikelihoods are (rounded): normal (-113); lognormal (-116); gamma (-111); weibull (-110). The Weibull model is a slightly better fit based on the log-likelihood.

</details>
